title: Is there a better way to filter results when adding item to Sales Invoice

posts.name: volkswagner
posts.cooked:
Even though there are several fields (item_name,description,item_group,customer_code) in the
"Search By" list of Search dialog box, we can’t combine data from multiple fields to narrow down item selection.

It looks like I would need a custom script to override the default filter to enable combining “product group” and “item name” fields to narrow search results.

Am I missing something?

I’m thinking perhaps a custom script that would override the default filter where we could input something like <item_group>:<item_description>. Since there’s no limitation on special characters in item_name and item_code, I think it would be hard to find a special character to separate the fields.

Other ideas:
Add a custom button [Advanced Search} in the “fetch items from” menu that would open a dialog with filters for ‘item_group’ and any other valuable filter fields.

Thoughts?

posts.name: volkswagner
posts.cooked:
@ahsantareen your Item Template looks like a great enhancement to ERPNext. I’m curious if you’re using the built-in Item Attributes for the fields in Item Template or if these fields are also custom.

Would you mind sharing your script for the “Item Group” button?

One thing that comes to mind is ease of use. Some users like the ability to stay on the keyboard (not bounce between keyboard and mouse) for data entry. Frappe’s child table has a nice feature when tabbing through the end of the row, will create a new row for rapid data entry.

Minor rant here… this is why I’m disappointed in Frappe’s decision to change the Description field type to rich text in V15 (it breaks the ability to tab to the next field). Changing the order of the fields (putting description before item_code) is a decent workaround. It’s key to be able to stay at the keyboard for data entry (as much as possible).

As I write this, I think one solution might be to create a custom field like “item_group:item_code” and/or “item_group:item_name”. This might allow the user to stay at the keyboard, but would likely need to type the entire group_name.

EDIT: I thought perhaps I could add item_group to the items child table of Sales Invoice. The field is by default readonly, and hidden. Maybe I can modify this and set the field to readonly, when item_code is not set, then for item_code include the item_group in the filter. This would need to be conditional on the item_group is not empty, otherwise the default filter behavior would be used.

Would this cause any circular reference?

In practice, I would probably exclude the item_group from the list view, but allow the user to click the pencil icon to utilize this function. I think the advanced search is only needed in a small percentage of cases, when staff have a good memory of product info (built muscle memory for data entry).
